page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-32 is a flexible virtual compute instance configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor running at a sustained clock speed of 3.6 GHz, each vCPU maps directly to a single execution thread on an independent physical core, eliminating resource contention inherent in simultaneous multithreading environments. The instance is allocated 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

Hardware design choices for this shape emphasize predictable compute throughput and execution consistency across multithreaded workloads. The platform includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and omits both integrated graphics acceleration and local NVMe storage, meaning persistent storage requirements must be handled externally via network-attached block volumes. Because the system runs on the arm64 architecture without x86-specific instruction sets, application stacks must be compiled natively for ARM64 to achieve optimal operational efficiency.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the Ampere-based ARM architecture provides dense, linear compute scaling with minimal per-core power consumption. The dedicated core topology ensures stable execution times for computational tasks compared to shared or hyperthreaded x86 architectures. This configuration is particularly suitable for compute-bound microservices, continuous integration build nodes, web application serving, and distributed containerized software deployments optimized for ARM64.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-32 is an ARM-based compute instance equipped with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Ampere AmpereOne-M processor operating at 3.6 GHz. Featuring a single thread per physical core, the instance provides predictable execution without multithreading contention. It is provisioned with 32.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server lacks local ephemeral storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage for disk operations. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With high single-thread clock frequencies and dedicated ARM64 execution pipelines, the platform delivers strong compute density and qualitative operating efficiency for parallelized workloads. The VM.Standard.A4.Flex.8-32 is well suited for compiled ARM64 application services, continuous integration build runners, microservices clusters, and compute-focused backend processing.
